Distance from Each Segment Down to the Nearest River

Source: R/frs_near_river.R
frs_near_river.Rd

For every segment of a segmented streams table that is smaller than a threshold, walks the network downstream and records the distance to the nearest segment at least that size. Size is one of three measures: mean annual discharge (mad_m3s), modelled channel width (channel_width) or stream order (stream_order). A habitat rule's near_river condition reads the result, so a small stream close to a large river can pass a rule whose size test it fails (see frs_habitat_predicates()). frs_habitat_classify() calls this itself when a rule asks; call it directly to inspect the distances.

Usage

frs_near_river(
  conn,
  table,
  to,
  threshold,
  distance_max,
  measure = "discharge",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

conn

A DBI::DBIConnection object (from frs_db_conn()).

table

Character. Schema-qualified segmented streams table with id_segment, watershed_group_code, blue_line_key, watershed_key, downstream_route_measure, wscode_ltree, localcode_ltree, edge_type, waterbody_key, length_metre, geom, and the column of each measure asked for: mad_m3s, channel_width or stream_order.

to

Character. Schema-qualified output table, created if it does not exist, with columns id_segment, watershed_group_code, measure, threshold, distance_max and dist_m. A near_river rule reads only rows of its own exact measure, threshold and distance, so build the table with the pairs the rules carry (frs_habitat_classify() does): a walk at a longer distance does not serve a rule with a shorter one. Rows for the watershed groups in table are replaced on every call; other groups' rows are kept. A table written by fresh 0.41.0 (with a discharge_min column and no measure) stops the call; drop it and re-run.

threshold

Numeric vector. River sizes to find, each finite and above zero, in the measure's unit: m3/s for "discharge", m for "channel_width", an order for "stream_order".

distance_max

Numeric vector, one per threshold. Farthest distance (m) to record for that pair. Each pair is walked on its own, so a pair's distances never depend on the other pairs in the call; pairs must be distinct.

measure

Character, length 1 or one per threshold: "discharge" (default), "channel_width" or "stream_order".

verbose

Logical. Print rows written, segments with no local code, and timing. Default TRUE.

Value

conn invisibly, for pipe chaining.

Details

The walk follows main flow (blue_line_key = watershed_key), as the other downstream traces in fresh do, so a side channel starts on the main stem below it.

Where the distance starts and ends.

  • It starts at the segment's downstream end, so a long segment whose lower end is within the distance passes whole.

  • It ends at the bank of the river, not at its centreline. Where a tributary meets a river drawn as a polygon, its line crosses the polygon as a connector (FWA edge types 1400 and 1450) to the centreline. A connector belongs to the tributary, so it is never a target, and the connector inside the target's polygon (same waterbody_key) is left out of the distance. FWA draws about a third of connectors as side lines, which the walk does not follow; the walk then jumps from the tributary's mouth to the centreline, and that jump is left out too. A connector inside a polygon the walk only passes through, because that river is too small, stays in the distance.

  • Any other jump between consecutive rows of the path is counted at its straight length: a side channel the walk does not follow, or a stretch of river outside table that the path leaves and re-enters.

  • Where a tributary joins its parent follows FWA's local codes, as in every downstream trace in fresh. Where a code places the confluence away from where the lines meet, the distance can differ from a walk that enters at the nearest point, either way: longer by a counted jump, or shorter by the stretch between the two points.

Which segments are measured. Only segments whose own value of the measure is NULL or below threshold get a row: a river large enough to be a target passes or fails on its own size test, never on its distance to itself. A segment with a NULL value is never a target.

The three measures differ in what they see. fwapg's discharge is missing on some main stems (none of BULK's 1,118 river-polygon rows carries one), while channel width is modelled on every river-polygon row and missing mostly on first-order streams, which are origins, not targets. Most lake flow lines carry no width but do carry an order, so under width a lake's line is rarely a river and under order it is. Stream order is topological: an order-5 stream in a dry basin can carry less water than an order-4 one in a wet basin.

Limits.

  • The walk sees only table. A working table holds one watershed group, so a river beyond the group's outlet is not found.

  • To stay fast, the walk joins only rows within distance_max (plus the longest connector run) in a straight line, and cuts the path where a row it skipped was directly above the next row on that row's line. A path that jumps out of that reach and comes back in a way that test cannot see (the skipped run ends a line, or the row above is out of step with its local code) can read short. It needs a jump between path rows; none occurs on BULK at 3 m3/s within 1 or 20 km.

  • A segment with no local watershed code (localcode_ltree NULL), which is most side channels (edge types 1100, 1150, 1350), has no place in FWA_Downstream()'s ordering. It never walks, so it gets no row and never passes on near_river. Their count is reported when verbose.

See also

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- frs_db_conn()

# Segments within 1 km of a river carrying 3 m3/s, BULK working table
frs_near_river(conn, "working_bulk.streams", "working_bulk.near_river",
  threshold = 3, distance_max = 1000)

# The same, finding the river by a modelled channel width of 20 m
frs_near_river(conn, "working_bulk.streams", "working_bulk.near_river",
  threshold = 20, distance_max = 1000, measure = "channel_width")

DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, "
  SELECT measure, threshold, count(*) AS n, round(avg(dist_m)) AS mean_m
  FROM working_bulk.near_river GROUP BY 1, 2")

DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
} # }
